Erin — thanks for the clarity. Below are two concrete configurations (ballpark pricing + assumptions) we can iterate on during tomorrow's call. Numbers assume English text, average prompt+completion = 60 tokens, model family X (medium-encoder) with Redwood's optimized runtime. Prices below are for inference-only (no fine-tuning).

Option A — Hosted (fast to get started)
- Target: p95 chat 300ms / scoring p95 200–250ms (hosted tail is higher due to multi-tenant queues)
- Unit price: $2,100 per 1M tokens (on estimated 600M/mo), includes KV prefix caching, standard batching.
- Notes: Streaming enabled reduces observable tail latency for interactive chat but adds ~5–10% CPU/GPU utilization overhead; cost increases ~8% vs non-streamed billing estimate because of less efficient batching.

Option B — Dedicated (reserved capacity) — recommended for strict p95 150ms
- Target: p95 scoring <= 150ms, chat p95 <= 300ms
- Unit price: $950 per 1M tokens with 12mo commit at 600M/mo (includes dedicated GPUs, tail-optimized scheduling, and aggressive KV caching).
- Tail optimization: dedicated pools allow smaller batch windows and pre-warmed KV caches which materially reduces p95.
- Streaming + micro-batching: enable streaming for scoring hot path + micro-batching (batch window 3–5ms) for chat; overall cost delta ~+4% over baseline dedicated estimate.

Quick unit economics (illustrative at 600M tokens/mo)
- Hosted: 600M/mo * $2,100/1M = $1,260,000 / month (this is illustrative; hosted list pricing steps down with volume).
- Dedicated: 600M/mo * $950/1M = $570,000 / month (with commit/discounting amortized across term).

Trade-offs summary:
- Hosted: fastest to launch, higher unit cost, tail latency higher due to multi-tenancy and batching for efficiency.
- Dedicated: lower unit cost at scale and better tail latency; requires commit and setup (short provisioning window).
- Streaming: reduces perceived tail but reduces batching efficiency; slight incremental cost, large benefit for interactive p95.

Attachments: updated pricing sheet (examples for 200/400/600/1,000M tokens) and an example MOP where we pin scoring on dedicated pool and route chat to hosted during spikes.

I'll come ready with a 1-page MAO and an estimated PO template tomorrow. For our call — could you confirm which of these configurations maps closest to your procurement comfort (Hosted for TTV vs Dedicated for cost+SLO)?

See you at 11:00 PT.

Best,
Marissa
